questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code records metrics for tickets? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Why are the open-ticket gauges backed by AtomicInteger instances stored in the openByPriority map rather than created inline and only handed to the registry?
choices: Because AtomicInteger is the only Number type that Micrometer gauges accept.
Because the map makes the gauge values thread-safe; the registry itself never reads them concurrently.
Because the registry holds only a weak reference to a gauged object, so the map keeps each counter alive and lets the service update it.
Because Micrometer would otherwise re-query the repository on every scrape, and the map caches the result.

questions.prompt: Given the enums in this code, what is the maximum number of distinct time series the support.tickets.created counter can produce?
choices: 12, one per priority and channel combination.
Unbounded, because every ticket creates a new series.

questions.prompt: Because of clock skew between nodes, firstResponse is called with a respondedAt that is slightly earlier than ticket.createdAt(). What does the code record?
choices: A zero-length sample in the timer and one SLA breach.
A negative sample in the timer, which lowers the reported mean latency.
An IllegalArgumentException from the timer, which the service lets propagate to the caller.
Nothing in the timer, because Micrometer ignores negative durations, and no breach is counted.
